🚀 Startup India, DPIIT in Karauli, Rajasthan

The TEJAS (Transforming Entrepreneurial Journeys Across States and Districts) Workshop was successfully conducted in Karauli, Rajasthan, bringing together government officials, academia and aspiring entrepreneurs to strengthen the district’s startup ecosystem and foster a culture of entrepreneurship.

Shri Aman Chaudhary, SDM, Karauli, graced the session and highlighted the Rajasthan State Government’s efforts to strengthen the state’s startup landscape and encourage young people to become job creators rather than job seekers.

Ms. Aveesha Kaur, Startup India, DPIIT, conducted an insightful session on the Startup India initiative, providing an overview of key schemes, regulatory benefits and available support, while equipping aspiring entrepreneurs with the knowledge to navigate the startup ecosystem and leverage government support.

An expert session, “Build for India,” featured Mr. Saurabh Jain, Advisor and former VP, Paytm, who delivered a special address on building solutions and ventures for India’s diverse and evolving market.

The workshop was followed by a panel discussion on “Preparing the Next Generation of Entrepreneurs: Future Skills, AI and District Innovation,” featuring Mr Pushpendra Singh, Founder, Shoonya Shikhar Gurukulam, and Mr Agrim Kumar Gupta, Founder, Utsavy. The discussion explored the role of future-ready skills, AI and district-level innovation in shaping the next generation of entrepreneurs.

✨ Key Highlights:
🚀 Session on Startup India initiatives, schemes and regulatory benefits
🏛️ Insights on Rajasthan’s vision for youth-led entrepreneurship
💡 Expert session on building innovative solutions for India
🤝 Panel discussion on future skills, AI and district innovation
🌱 Strengthening entrepreneurship and startup opportunities at the district level

The discussion had the presence of startups and park companies— Laurus Labs Limited, Huwel Lifesciences, 𝗕𝘆𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗽𝗲𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗣𝘃𝘁 𝗟𝘁𝗱, Footryx Healthcare Pvt Ltd, and 𝗖𝗿𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗵𝗶𝘅 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗣𝘃𝘁 𝗟𝘁𝗱—to platform their innovations and explore opportunities for international partnerships and market access.

Held at ICRISAT, the programme converged 44 mid-to-senior professionals from 20 countries across the Global South for a two-week learning experience focused on technology transfer, including the application of AI in research, scientific communication, and data analysis.

As Chief Guest, Dr. Dash shared remarks on the importance of collaboration among the Global South countries and joined the ICRISAT leadership team in presenting certificates to the participants, marking the culmination of their learning journey.

Earlier in the programme, our colleague Dr. Vithal K Lakkineni, Ph.D. engaged with the participants and shared practical perspectives on “𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀, 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗚𝗹𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗹 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗵 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻,” highlighting the importance of partnerships and collaborative approaches in advancing innovation across emerging ecosystems.

We are pleased to support platforms that foster global knowledge exchange, technology transfer, and innovation capacity-building across the Global South.

We congratulate ICRISAT and all the participants on the successful completion of the programme and wish them continued success as they apply their learnings to advance innovation and technology transfer in their respective countries.

In India, timely respiratory support could help prevent 80% of newborn deaths linked to respiratory distress syndrome. 

And this is where Saans, a C-CAMP-supported innovation, is making a life-saving difference!

SAANS, an innovation by C-CAMP startup @InnAccel, is expanding easy access to critical respiratory care for newborns — not just in urban areas, but also in low-resource and remote settings across India and beyond.

It is a non-invasive, portable CPAP technology that delivers continuous positive airway pressure while monitoring Oxygen and airflow in real time, without relying on complex infrastructure.

Check out this video by @GatesIndia to see how this innovation is expanding access to newborn respiratory care.

India’s next AI story may not just be about what machines can generate. It may be about what they can see, understand, and act on in the physical world.

We are proud to share that Constems-AI Systems (CAI) has been featured in Outlook Publishing (India) Pvt. Ltd.’s 15th August Special Edition, highlighting our vision for building Native Vision AI from India for the world.

The feature, "The Next Leap In AI Will Be Vision, And It Is Being Built In India," spotlights the vision and journey of Amit Srivastava, Co-Founder & CTO at Constems-AI, and Amit Singh, Co-Founder & CEO at Constems-AI, and their commitment to building proprietary Vision AI technology from India.

At the heart of their vision is a clear belief: industries generate visual signals every second, but much of that information remains difficult to interpret and act on in real time. Constems-AI is working to change this by enabling enterprises to turn visual information into decision-ready intelligence.

From retail and manufacturing to agriculture, logistics, healthcare, and infrastructure, our Vision AI solutions are designed for real-world enterprise environments across edge, cloud, and on-premises deployments.

For us, building AI in India is also about building ownership of the technology, from foundation models and inference engines to deployment architecture and enterprise applications. Our ambition goes beyond adopting the global AI wave; it is about contributing technology from India that can serve industries worldwide.

As India marks its 80th Independence Day, this recognition makes the moment especially meaningful. We remain committed to a future where India is not only a major adopter of AI but also a creator of the technologies shaping it.

Thank you to Outlook for featuring the Constems-AI story and recognising the vision behind our journey.

Day 3 | Partnerships, Fundraising Readiness & Founder Evolution

The final day of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program focused on building long-term scale engines - partnerships, investor readiness, and leadership evolution.

We began with “Channel & Partnerships: Designing a Partner Engine That Scales,” led by Venkat Shyam. Founders explored how structured channel #strategies, aligned incentives, and ecosystem #collaborations can unlock non-linear growth beyond direct sales.

In the #Fundraising Deep Dive: #Investor-Grade Company — From Pitch to Process & Metrics That Raise Money, Ravindra Krishnappa emphasized building companies that are investment-ready by design. The session broke down traction KPIs, investors' trust, #governance discipline, narrative clarity, and process maturity.

The program concluded with “Org & Leadership for Scaling: Founder-to-CEO Transition” led by Sathyanarayana B V, followed by final reflections and key takeaways. The conversation centered on building leadership depth, creating accountable org structures, and evolving from operator to strategic decision-maker. Sathyanarayana B V also spoke about #HR Management Grid, Leadership styles, how each one of them affects and has an impact in different workplaces, and how leaders are born or lost under different #leadership style

Scaling a startup ultimately requires more than #strategy - it demands founder transformation.

We thank all our expert #mentors and participating #founders for making this acceleration journey deeply insightful and impact-driven. At DERBI Foundation, our commitment remains clear: enabling startups with the right #ecosystem, right #frameworks, and right #mentorship to scale sustainably.

Day 2 | Expanding Markets, Strengthening Financial Foundations

Day 2 of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program shifted the lens from internal readiness to external expansion and financial resilience.

The day opened with “Market Access Strategy: #IndiaExpansion + Global Entry Readiness” led by Shivi Jain. Startups explored structured approaches to entering new markets, from regulatory preparedness and localization strategy to channel partnerships and #global positioning. The focus was on building scalable access, not opportunistic expansion.

In the Cashflow & Working Capital War-Room: Scale Without Dying, Nayak guided founders through one of the most underestimated growth levers — liquidity discipline. Through real-world scenarios and financial stress-testing frameworks, startups examined burn cycles, receivables management, and #capital efficiency as core survival metrics.

The day concluded with “Deal Structuring & Term Sheet Masterclass: Don’t Lose the Company” by Sharath Shyamasunder, The Startup Zone, where founders unpacked #investor clauses, dilution mechanics, control rights, and long-term implications of #fundraising decisions.

Growth is exciting. But #sustainable scale is built on informed expansion, disciplined capital management, and smart deal-making.

Two of the ten innovations recognised in the H&M Foundation's Global Change Award 2026 are companies we have backed at Social Alpha.

https://lnkd.in/gAtXh9jX

CanvaLoop, whose Agro-Lyocell turns agricultural residue into regenerated cellulosic fibre — a forest-free alternative to the wood that conventional viscose still consumes.

Microbeworks Scientific, whose MicroBlue produces biodegradable dyes through microbial fermentation, is engineered to run on the dyeing infrastructure the industry already owns rather than demanding it be rebuilt.

Fashion's footprint will not be fixed by pledges, capsule collections, or the word "sustainable" stretched until it means nothing. It will be fixed by people willing to carry hard science out of the laboratory and onto the factory floor — and to absorb the translational risk that journey demands.

That is the work. It is slow, unglamorous, and rarely rewarded by the narrative economy. A prize like this matters because, for once, it points the spotlight at the right thing.

Congratulations to both teams. The recognition is earned. The harder part — deployment at scale — is what we get to do next, together.

Social Alpha Sustain Plus

Storing more energy, safely and efficiently, requires more than better batteries–it requires the right technologies to manage, test and ready them for markets. 
From advanced Battery Management Systems (BMS) to new chemistries like sodium-ion and zinc-based batteries, the next generation of energy storage is being shaped by innovators rethinking conventional technologies. 

At Social Alpha, we help these innovations move from the lab to the market. Through access to testing infrastructure, funding, pilots and industry partnerships, we work alongside science-led founders to turn innovation market-ready. 

Read our latest article by Ahmad Ali exploring the journey of battery innovations from lab to market and Social Alpha’s critical role in facilitating this move.

Looking to upskill your students, trainees, or technical team?
A standard, off-the-shelf training doesn't always fit every team’s unique technical needs. That’s why we design bespoke, practical hands-on workshops tailored to your specific research goals, operational workflows, and skill levels.

"𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐭𝐨𝐭𝐲𝐩𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐬𝐞."

We had a valuable session discussing how early-stage founders can turn a working prototype into an investor-ready business.

Here are the key takeaways from the discussion:

 🛠️ BUILD – Create a solid foundation and a product of true value.
 📊 PROVE – Validate your concept and establish clear market fit.
 🤝 SELL – Get your solution out there and into the hands of customers.
 🔄 REPEAT – Standardize your winning process and execute consistently.
 📈 COMPOUND – Let the momentum build and watch your consistent efforts multiply over time.

It's a great reminder that sustainable growth isn't about skipping steps; it's about mastering the cycle.

A special thanks to our guest speaker, Karthik K.R.G, PhD  for sharing his experience and practical advice with our founders.

Thank you to all the founders and entrepreneurs who attended and made it such an interactive discussion.

Stay tuned for more upcoming events and resources from Cultiv8.

Srisakthi Karthikeyan Anuvind Jayan

This is the work iCreate exists for: helping India's innovators cross that exact bridge.
